claude.result:
33 tests pass (up from 26, the 7 new threshold tests all pass); the only 2 failures are the pre-existing unrelated ones. Implementation is complete.

## Summary

Added `--threshold <metric=min>` support to `frai eval`, with the core logic in `frai-core`:

**`packages/frai-core/src/eval/index.js`** — `generateReport` now accepts an optional `thresholds` object (`{ exact_match: 0.9 }`). It validates each entry (min must be a number in `[0, 1]`; metric id must exist among the evaluated metrics — the error lists valid ids), then adds top-level `passed` and a `thresholds` array (`{ metric, min, score, passed }`) to the report. A metric with a `null`/missing score fails its threshold rather than crashing. Invalid input throws the new exported `ThresholdValidationError`. Works for custom metrics too, since it only reads `evaluations[].id`/`.score`.

**`packages/frai-core/src/eval/reporters.js`** — Markdown reports gain a "Thresholds" section (overall PASS/FAIL plus one line per metric) when `report.thresholds` is present.

**`packages/frai-cli/src/index.ts`** — new repeatable `--threshold` option; `runEvalCommand` parses `<metric>=<min>` strings (malformed syntax throws the same `ThresholdValidationError`), passes the resulting object to `generateReport`, and:
- exits 2 with a descriptive message and **no report written** on `ThresholdValidationError` (malformed value or unknown metric),
- exits 1 if the report's `passed` is `false`,
- otherwise behaves exactly as before (report written, exit 0).

Also updated both READMEs' `frai eval` docs and added threshold test coverage in `frai-core`. Verified manually via the built CLI (baseline, pass, fail, no-score, malformed, unknown-metric, out-of-range, and Markdown cases) and via `pnpm --filter frai-core test`/`tsc --noEmit` — all pass except the two pre-existing unrelated failures (`governance.test.js` and the default-evaluations toxicity assertion) that were already broken on `main`.
